S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers shall report every confirmed thermal event involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal injury to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of confirmation, and provide a complete incident report within 10 business days. They shall notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident indicates a credible product-specific safety risk or requires customer action.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Manufacturers shall submit per-model results and sample sizes to the regulator; these individual-company results shall not be publicly disclosed. A failure rate above 5% requires a corrective-action plan submitted to the regulator and follow-up testing within 12 months; it does not by itself require market withdrawal.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units shall support secure remote emergency shut-off by 24 months after adoption, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and a clear customer notification and manual override procedure. Manufacturers shall retrofit already-installed units to support remote shut-off within 6 years after adoption where technically feasible; where retrofitting is infeasible, they shall provide an equivalent documented risk-reduction measure and notify affected customers.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery units shall include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after adoption. Manufacturers shall provide regulators with evidence that the suppression system is effective and does not introduce new hazards.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer shall promptly notify regulators and affected customers. Regulators shall assess the evidence and may require corrective action, suspension, or recall, including a recall where warranted by the risk.

document.section_notes: The final S2 sets no permanent numeric limit and no sales stop, so a model above 5% can remain on sale indefinitely after a corrective-action plan; per-model results go to regulators and, through S5, to purchasers. S5 makes recall discretionary rather than mandatory at 8 incidents per 100,000, with customer notice within 48 hours. S4 requires built-in suppression within 36 months, and S3 sets a 6-year retrofit deadline with an alternative-measure escape.
